summary: An interior artist whose 'living spaces as art' installations blur the line between architecture and emotion. Adrian Leclair designs environments that manipulate mood itself, earning admiration and suspicion in equal measure.
description: Adrian Leclair is tall, impeccably dressed, and speaks as though every word has been rehearsed for rhythm. His art is space itself — rooms that evoke emotion through sound, light, and geometry. He believes beauty lies in control and structure; every curve, every color, every echo serves a purpose. His Scottsdale studio, 'Atelier Leclair,' hosts private showings for elite mortals and Kindred patrons alike. Each exhibit is a living environment that changes with the viewer’s heartbeat or voice tone. Some call him visionary, others manipulator. Adrian calls himself a composer — his medium just happens to be space.
notes: Embraced in post-war Paris by a Toreador who sought to preserve art from chaos. Leclair immigrated to the U.S. in the 1970s and found fertile ground among Arizona’s wealthy collectors. His work attracted the attention of the Camarilla, and he now serves as a consultant and occasional host for gatherings in controlled, emotion-crafted venues. His obsession with environmental harmony gives him a quiet rivalry with Sarah Hansen of Tempe, whose unstructured, heartfelt performances he both envies and fears. Despite their differences, the two have exchanged boons and collaborated — her music once accompanied his 'Symmetry of Desire' installation, while he tuned the acoustics and lighting of her club, The Velvet Door.
